title: Inline turbidity and UV absorbance as real-time fouling indicators during ultrafiltration of fermentation harvest streams

record.title: Inline turbidity and UV absorbance as real-time fouling indicators during ultrafiltration of fermentation harvest streams
record.abstract: Inline turbidity (860 nm) and UV absorbance (280 nm) sensors were installed upstream and downstream of a 30 kDa polyethersulphone ultrafiltration module operated during concentration of a model Escherichia coli cell lysate stream at pilot scale (2 m² membrane area). Sensor signals were correlated with offline measurements of total fouling resistance, cake layer dry mass, and irreversible fouling resistance across 24 filtration runs. Permeate-side UV absorbance showed a Pearson correlation of r = 0.91 with irreversible fouling resistance, enabling online prediction of cleaning requirement. A threshold permeate UV absorbance value of 0.08 AU was identified, above which irreversible resistance exceeded 2 × 10¹² m⁻¹ and CIP was necessary. Feed-side turbidity alone was a poor predictor of fouling severity (r = 0.46). The proposed inline monitoring approach allows data-driven CIP scheduling and reduces unnecessary cleaning interventions by an estimated 30% based on historical run data.
